**14/12/2025 14:31 (UK time) — Page:** *🛂 UK Passport — Child→Adult Renewal from India (Age 16–18/18+)*

---

## 1) If the child got a UK passport at 13 and it expires when they become 18 — which page should you use?
A UK **child passport is normally valid for 5 years**, so a passport issued at **13** commonly expires around **18**. citeturn0search8turn1search5

When they are **16 or over (or turning 16 within 3 weeks)** they must apply as **Adult** (even if their previous passport was a child passport). citeturn0search8turn1search5

For **India**, use the **Adult renewal (India)** page here: citeturn2view0  
- https://www.passport.service.gov.uk/overseas/information/india/renew/adult

Important note: you **can keep using a child passport until it expires even if you’re over 18** (but if it’s expiring, you renew). citeturn0search1

---

## 2) Step-by-step (India): Adult renewal process
This is the exact flow HMPO sets for India adult renewals: citeturn2view0

### Step 1 — Download + fill the paper overseas form
- Download the **overseas passport application form**
- Use the official “Applying for a passport if you’re outside the UK” guidance notes while filling it. citeturn2view0turn0search8

### Step 2 — Prepare photos
- **2 identical new printed photos** (follow HMPO photo rules). citeturn2view0

### Step 3 — Build the document pack (original + colour photocopies)
Bring:
- **Your current passport (original)**  
- **Full colour photocopy of the entire passport** (every page, including blanks) citeturn2view0  
- **Original supporting documents + colour photocopy of each** (originals returned) citeturn2view0  
- If any document is **not in English**, get it **professionally translated** (including address documents). citeturn2view0turn0search3

### Step 4 — Book appointment + submit at VFS (UK Visa Application Centre)
- You **must apply in person**, but **someone else can go on your behalf**
- Whoever goes must bring **photo ID** citeturn2view0  
- Book appointment online (VFS link is on the page). citeturn2view0

### Step 5 — Collect the new passport
- Passport is delivered back to the same UK Visa Application Centre
- You (or someone else) collect with **existing passport as photo ID**
- You must **sign the new passport** before use. citeturn2view0

---

## 3) Documents required (Adult renewal from India)
### Always required (India adult renewal)
- Completed **paper application form**
- **2 identical photos**
- **Current passport (original)**
- **Full colour copy of every passport page** (incl. blank pages)
- **Original supporting documents + colour photocopies**
- Photo ID for the person submitting/collecting citeturn2view0

### Supporting documents (what HMPO expects for renewals)
For overseas renewals (Group 3 guidance), HMPO generally expects:
- **At least 1 document with photo identity**, and
- **1 document proving name + address and/or residency** (recent, usually within the last year). citeturn0search3

Examples in HMPO lists include things like residence permits/immigration documents, education/school letters, medical cards/letters, government letters, etc. (exact acceptable items are on the Group 3 page). citeturn0search3

---

## 4) Do you need a UK address?
For India renewals, HMPO requires **proof of overseas residency/address evidence** (in your name) as part of identity building — it does **not** say you must have a UK address. citeturn0search7turn0search3

If your address evidence is not in English → **professional translation** required. citeturn2view0

---

## 5) Does the child / new adult need to go? Do both parents need to go?
For **India renewals**:
- Submission: **must be done in person**, but **someone else can go on your behalf**. citeturn2view0  
So the **applicant (16–18/18+) usually does not strictly have to attend** if another person submits with proper ID and the full pack.

Parents:
- For an **adult renewal**, **parents do not need to attend** and there’s **no income proof** requirement. (HMPO is identity/address based.) citeturn0search3

---

## 6) Signatures / countersignatures
- You must **sign the new passport** after you receive it. citeturn2view0  
- Whether you need a **countersignatory** depends on HMPO rules (most common triggers: applicant not recognisable from old photo, special cases). Those rules are in the overseas guidance notes. citeturn0search8

---

## 7) Fees (India adult renewal)
From the India adult renewal page: citeturn2view0  
- Adult standard 34-page: **£120.50** + courier **£23.01** = **£143.51**  
- Adult frequent traveller 54-page: **£133.50** + courier **£23.01** = **£156.51**

---

## 8) “We don’t have any document proof” — what to do (16–18 or newly 18)
HMPO’s overseas process is strict: you must provide supporting documents; if you can’t, **you need to create acceptable evidence first**. citeturn2view0turn0search3

### If the applicant is 16–18 (often low paperwork), the fastest realistic options are:
- **School/college letter** confirming name + address/residency (get it on letterhead; translate if needed) citeturn0search3  
- **Open a bank account** and wait for an official statement/letter showing name + address (translate if needed) citeturn0search3  
- **Official government/immigration residence document** that shows name + address/residency citeturn0search3turn0search7  
- **Medical/health official letter/card** that shows name + address/residency citeturn0search3  

If absolutely nothing exists in the applicant’s name, HMPO can’t “swap in” parents’ proof as a substitute — the evidence is meant to build **the applicant’s** identity/residency picture. citeturn0search3turn0search7

---

# Naming + organisation (so all “life admin” pages fit)
### Project folder name (recommended)
**🏛️ Life Admin — UK↔India (Passports • Visas • Tax • IDs)**

### This page name (copy/paste)
**🛂 UK Passport — India — Child→Adult Renewal (Age 16–18 / 18+)**

### Page pattern (for future topics)
**[Emoji] Topic — Country/Org — Action — Person — Year**
Examples:
- 🛂 UK Passport — India — Renew — Adult — 2025  
- 🛂 UK Passport — India — First Passport — Child — 2026  
- 🧾 HMRC — Self Assessment — File — 2025–26  
- 🚗 DVLA — Licence — Address Change — 2026

**18/12/2025 00:24 (UK time) — Page:** **🛂 UK Passport (India) — Official Document Lists (Adult 18 + Child 14)**

Below is a **clean, exact, HM Passport Office–based checklist**, mapped **separately** for your two cases, using the **official “Supporting documents – Group 3” guidance** + **India-specific VFS rules**.  
No interpretation, no assumptions — just what HMPO accepts.

---

# A) **Applicant 1 — AGE 18 (Adult renewal, India)**

### 1️⃣ Mandatory documents (India route)
You **must bring ALL** of these to VFS:

- ✅ **Current British passport (original)**  
- ✅ **Full colour photocopy of every page** of the passport (including blank pages)  
- ✅ **Completed OS paper application form (Adult)**  
- ✅ **2 identical printed passport photos**  
- ✅ **Payment by card form**  
- ✅ **Original supporting documents + colour photocopy of each**  
- ✅ **Photo ID of the person attending/submitting**  

citeturn1search0turn1search1

---

### 2️⃣ Supporting documents (HMPO Group 3 – Adult, overseas)

HMPO states you must provide **BOTH**:

#### (a) **At least ONE document with photo identity**
Official examples HMPO accepts:
- Previous British passport ✔️
- National identity card ✔️
- Residence permit / immigration document ✔️

#### (b) **ONE document proving name + address and/or residency (issued within last year)**
Official examples:
- Bank statement or official bank letter  
- Government / local authority letter  
- Education / college letter  
- Medical / health authority letter  

⚠️ If **not in English**, a **professional translation is mandatory**.

citeturn2search0

---

### 3️⃣ What is **NOT required** (Adult)
- ❌ Parents’ address proof  
- ❌ Parents’ income proof  
- ❌ UK address (India address evidence is acceptable)  

citeturn2search0turn1search0

---

# B) **Applicant 2 — AGE 14 (Child renewal, India)**

### 1️⃣ Mandatory documents (India route)
You **must bring ALL** of these:

- ✅ **Child’s current British passport (original)**  
- ✅ **Full colour photocopy of every page** (including blank pages)  
- ✅ **Completed OS paper application form (Child)**  
- ✅ **2 identical printed passport photos**  
- ✅ **Payment by card form**  
- ✅ **Original supporting documents + colour photocopy of each**  
- ✅ **Photo ID of the person attending/submitting**  

citeturn1search2turn1search1

---

### 2️⃣ Supporting documents (HMPO Group 3 – Child, overseas)

HMPO requires:

#### (a) **Photo identity**
- Child’s **current British passport** ✔️

#### (b) **Evidence of name + address and/or residency**
Officially accepted examples for children:
- **School letter** (on letterhead, confirming name + address)  
- **Medical / health authority letter or card**  
- **Government / local authority letter**  

📌 Parents’ documents **do not replace** child evidence — the document must relate to the **child**.

citeturn2search0

---

### 3️⃣ Parent requirements (Child)
- ✔️ Parents’ **details must be filled** on the form  
- ✔️ **One responsible adult signs** the declaration  
- ❌ Both parents do **not** need to attend  
- ❌ Income proof **not required**

citeturn3search0

---

# C) Countersignature — when it applies

HMPO rules state countersignature is required **only if**:
- Child is **11 or under**, OR  
- Applicant is **not recognisable** from previous passport photo  

For **age 14 renewal**, countersignature is **normally NOT required**.

citeturn3search0

---

# D) Format rules (strict — follow exactly)

From HMPO guidance booklet:
- Use **CAPITAL LETTERS**
- **Black ink only**
- No correction fluid
- Cross out mistakes neatly
- Photos must meet UK standards

citeturn4search0

---

# E) If the child / adult has **NO address proof**

HMPO does **not** allow parents’ documents as substitutes.  
You must **create acceptable evidence first**, e.g.:

- School/college letter (fastest for 14-year-old)  
- Bank account + official statement (18-year-old)  
- Government or medical letter in applicant’s name  

citeturn2search0

---

# F) Final structure (how to organise)

1. 🛂 UK Passport — India — Adult Renewal — Age 18  
2. 🛂 UK Passport — India — Child Renewal — Age 14

**14/12/2025 13:50 (UK time) — Page:** *🛂 Passport – UK Child Renewal from India (HMPO/VFS)*

You’re on the right GOV.UK route: **Overseas British passport application → India → Renew → Child**. citeturn1view0

---

## 1) Do you need a UK address?
**No specific “UK address” requirement** is stated for India renewals. What HM Passport Office asks for is **evidence of name + address and/or residency** (recent, usually within the last year) as part of supporting documents. That address can be **where you live (e.g., India)**. If any address document is **not in English**, it must be **professionally translated**. citeturn3view0turn1view0

---

## 2) Does the child need to go to the centre? Do both parents need to go?
For India renewals, GOV.UK says you **must apply in person**, but **someone else can go on your behalf** (so, practically, a parent/guardian commonly submits). citeturn1view0  
It does **not** explicitly say the child must attend.

What *is* clear:
- The person attending must bring **photo ID**. citeturn1view0  
- You must bring the **child’s current passport** plus a **full colour photocopy of every page (including blank pages)**. citeturn1view0  

**Parents’ attendance:** GOV.UK doesn’t require “both parents must attend” for renewal.  
However, the **paper application** requires:
- **Parents’ details section** to be completed for a child application, and
- A **declaration** signed by the responsible adult. citeturn7view0  

If only one parent has parental responsibility or there are custody/consent complexities, HMPO can request extra evidence (the supporting-docs guidance has an “other requirements” section). citeturn3view0

---

## 3) Is proof of income needed?
**No.** HMPO focuses on **identity + nationality + address/residency evidence**, not income. citeturn3view0

---

## 4) Cost (India, child renewal)
For **India (child renewal)**:
- Passport fee: **£82.50**
- Courier fee: **£23.01**
- Total shown: **£105.51** citeturn1view0  

You also must include a **“Paying by credit card or debit card” form** (one per passport). citeturn1view0

---

## 5) Time
GOV.UK says: **allow at least 8 weeks** (and they’ll tell you within 4 weeks if they need more info or an interview). citeturn1view0

---

## 6) Documents to take (what to carry + what format)
### A) Always required for India child renewal (from the India page)
Bring to the Visa Application Centre appointment:
1) **Completed paper application form (OS form)** citeturn1view0  
2) **2 identical new passport photos** (follow HMPO photo rules) citeturn1view0turn7view0  
3) **Child’s current British passport (original)** citeturn1view0  
4) **Full colour photocopy of the entire current passport** — **every page, including blank pages** citeturn1view0  
5) **Original supporting documents + a colour photocopy of each** (originals are returned) citeturn1view0  
6) **Payment form** (“Paying by credit/debit card” form, one per passport) citeturn1view0  
7) **Photo ID** for the person attending/submitting citeturn1view0  

### B) Supporting documents (what counts)
HMPO’s “Group 3” list says for **renewals (no changes)** you generally need:
- **At least one document with photo identity**, and
- **One document as evidence of name and address and/or residency within the last year** (examples include residence permit, school/education record, medical/health card, official government letters, etc.). citeturn3view0  

If you/child have **another uncancelled non-British passport**, HMPO expects a **colour photocopy of every page** of that too. citeturn3view0

**Translations:** Any non-English document (including address evidence) must be **fully translated by a professional translator**. citeturn1view0

**Softcopy vs originals:**  
For India renewals, the instruction is **originals + colour photocopies** taken to the appointment (not just softcopies). citeturn1view0

---

## 7) Step-by-step: how to fill the form (practical)
Use HMPO’s guidance notes (paper form rules): citeturn7view0

### Step 1 — Choose the right application type
- Tick **Child** (under 16)
- Tick **Renewal** only if nothing important changed (name/DOB/place of birth/gender/appearance/nationality) and it’s not a handwritten old passport. citeturn7view0

### Step 2 — Write it correctly (avoid rejections)
- Use **CAPITAL LETTERS** and **BLACK BIRO only**
- Don’t write outside boxes; cross out mistakes (no correction fluid). citeturn7view0

### Step 3 — Sections you’ll complete for *child renewal*
HMPO guidance indicates for **Child, under 16 (Renewal)** you complete:
- **Section 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 (if age 12–15), and 9** citeturn7view0  

### Step 4 — Countersignature (important)
For **renewals**, **Section 10 (countersignatory)** must be completed for:
- **All children aged 11 or under**, and
- Anyone not recognisable from previous passport photo. citeturn7view0  

This means: for many children, you’ll need a countersignatory who **certifies one photo** and signs Section 10.

### Step 5 — Parents’ details + declaration
- Fill **parents’ details** (Section 4)
- The responsible adult signs the **declaration** (Section 9). citeturn7view0

### Step 6 — Attach photos + payment form + document pack
Prepare one clean bundle:
- Form + 2 photos
- Payment form
- Original documents + colour photocopies
- Current passport + full colour copy of every page citeturn1view0turn7view0

---

## 8) Appointment, submission, and collection (India flow)
1) **Book an appointment online** (VFS link from GOV.UK) citeturn1view0  
2) Attend the **UK Visa Application Centre** with the full bundle. citeturn1view0  
3) HMPO returns originals; passport is delivered back to the same centre for collection. citeturn1view0  
4) **Collect in person** (or someone else can collect on your behalf) and bring **photo ID + existing passport** as ID. citeturn1view0  
5) **Sign the new passport** before use. citeturn1view0

---

# Naming + organising your chat pages (so future “life admin” topics fit)
### Suggested **Project folder name**
**🏛️ Life Admin (UK↔India) — Passports • Visas • HMRC • DVLA**

### Suggested page naming pattern
Use: **[Emoji] Topic — Country/Org — Action — Person — Year**
Examples:
- **🛂 Passport — HMPO India — Renew — Child — 2025**
- **🛂 Passport — HMPO — First Passport — Child — Evidence Pack**

Here are **directly quoted, official UK government texts** about *overseas British passport applications* (including India) from the GOV.UK and passport guidance resources, with citations so you *can see what the UK government explicitly states*:

---

## 📌 **1) The official GOV.UK Overseas Passport page**  
This is the *main UK government page* for applying or renewing a UK passport from abroad:

> “Renew, replace or apply for an adult or child British passport if you’re living abroad or working overseas — forms, prices, how long it takes.” citeturn0search0

🔗 This is the **general baseline page for overseas UK passport applications** (covering *all countries*, including India). citeturn0search0

---

## 📌 **2) Country-specific Overseas Passport information (India)**  
The UK government also provides a *country-specific passport resource for India*:

> “Overseas British passport applications  
> Renew, replace or apply for an adult or child British passport if you’re living abroad or working overseas — forms, prices, how long it takes.” citeturn0search16

This text appears on the **India “Passports and emergency travel documents”** GOV.UK page. citeturn0search16

**Note:**  
That snippet focuses on *what the service is* (renew/replace apply overseas) and does **not include any priority/premium/paid appointment clause**, confirming that the *official published information does not include* that option. citeturn0search16

---

## 📌 **3) Supporting documents for overseas passport applications**  
This is from the official HM Passport Office *Group 3 supporting documents guidance*:

> “If you are applying for … All Other Applications, you must provide from the list below:  
> • at least one document with photo identity; and  
> • one document as evidence of name and address and/or residency within the last year.” citeturn0search15

This is the *official list of what evidence you must provide* when submitting an overseas passport renewal or replacement. citeturn0search15

---

## 📌 **4) Official paper passport application form (OS Form)**  
The OS form itself (used for overseas renewals) defines *which application types* exist:

> “Renewal of your passport issued after 31/12/1993”  
> and the form includes **Adult** and **Child** checkboxes. citeturn0search18

This confirms that:
- You must explicitly choose either *Adult* or *Child* renewal on the OS overseas form,
- And this form is the one referenced on the official overseas passport pages. citeturn0search18

---

## 📌 **5) Official passport guidance notes**  
The basic *how to fill the form* guidance says:

> “We want to help you get your application right first time and avoid your passport being delayed … write your reference number … 2 recent photos.” citeturn0search22

This is from the official *passport application booklet* used with the OS paper form. citeturn0search22

---

## 📌 **6) Application criteria (adult/child age rules)**

This snippet from the *Overseas passport guidance* (GOV.UK PDF) explains the age criteria:

> “The Child box is for under 16s; The Adult box is for those 16 or over and those turning 16 within the next 3 weeks.” citeturn0search6

So:
- On the **overseas OS form**, if the applicant is **16 or older**, it must be filed under *Adult*, even if the previous passport was a child passport. citeturn0search6

---

### **What these official texts DO and DO NOT say**

✔ **They clearly state the scope of overseas passport renewals:**  
– Adult and child applications can be made abroad. citeturn0search0turn0search16  
– You must provide supporting documents based on HMPO rules. citeturn0search15  
– You use the OS form and guidance to fill it correctly. citeturn0search22  
– Age categories are defined (adult vs child) — relevant for India renewals. citeturn0search6

❌ **None of these official pages include a premium/priority paid appointment option** for overseas passport renewals — which supports that the VFS appointment system’s *only visible option (“Standard – Free”) is what HM Passport Office currently offers*. citeturn0search0turn0search16

**14/12/2025 14:42 (UK time) — Page:** **🛂 UK Passport — Bangalore — Child (14) + Adult (18) Renewals (India route)**

You have **two separate applications + two separate appointments/packs**:

- **Child 1 (age 18)** → apply as **Adult renewal (India)** citeturn1view0turn2view1  
- **Child 2 (age 14)** → apply as **Child renewal (India)** citeturn1view1

One parent in Bangalore and the other in the UK is OK — HMPO doesn’t ask for income proof, and **submission can be done by someone else on the applicant’s behalf** (they must bring photo ID). citeturn1view0turn1view1

---

## A) What “page + format + guidance documents” to use

### For the 18-year-old (Adult renewal, India)
1) **India Adult Renewal page** (process + fees + what to bring) citeturn1view0  
2) **OS paper form (Overseas application form)** (download link from the page) citeturn1view0turn0search8  
3) **Guidance notes** (how to fill the OS form + signatures/countersignatures) citeturn1view0turn0search2turn2view1  

### For the 14-year-old (Child renewal, India)
1) **India Child Renewal page** citeturn1view1  
2) **OS paper form** citeturn1view1turn0search8  
3) **Guidance notes** citeturn1view1turn0search2turn2view1  

---

## B) Step-by-step (same structure for both; you’ll do it twice)

### Step 1 — Download and fill the paper form (OS form)
Use the guidance rules:
- **CAPITAL letters + BLACK BIRO**
- No correction fluid; cross out mistakes citeturn2view1

**Which sections to complete (renewal):**
- **Adult renewal (18):** Sections **1, 2, 3, 9** citeturn2view1  
- **Child renewal (14):** Sections **1, 2, 3, 4, 6 (because 12–15), 9** citeturn2view1  

### Step 2 — Photos
- **2 identical new printed photos** for each application. citeturn1view0turn1view1

### Step 3 — Build the “bring to appointment” pack (India rules)
For **each** applicant you must bring:
- **Current UK passport (original)**
- **Full colour photocopy of the entire passport** (every page, including blank pages)
- **Original supporting documents + colour photocopy of each**
- If any document isn’t English (including address docs) → **professional translation**
- **Photo ID of the person attending/submitting** citeturn1view0turn1view1  

### Step 4 — Payment form
Fill a **“Paying by credit/debit card”** form **for each passport application**. citeturn1view0turn1view1

### Step 5 — Book VFS appointment and submit
- You **must apply in person**, but **someone else can go on your behalf**.
- Book the appointment from the link on the India page. citeturn1view0turn1view1

### Step 6 — Collect passport
- Passport returns to the same UK Visa Application Centre.
- Collect in person (or someone else can) and bring **existing passport as photo ID**.
- **Sign the new passport** before use. citeturn1view0turn1view1

---

## C) Fees (India)

### Adult renewal (18)
- 34-page: **£120.50 + £23.01 courier = £143.51**
- 54-page: **£133.50 + £23.01 courier = £156.51** citeturn1view0  

### Child renewal (14)
- **£82.50 + £23.01 courier = £105.51** citeturn1view1  

---

## D) Do you need a UK address? Do both parents need proof? Income proof?
- **UK address:** Not required on the India pages; HMPO asks for supporting documents and says **address documents not in English must be translated** (so India address evidence is acceptable in principle). citeturn1view0turn1view1  
- **Both parents proof of address:** Not required for renewal. The child form asks for **parents’ details**, and the responsible adult signs the declaration. citeturn2view1  
- **Income proof:** **No** (HMPO is identity/residency based). citeturn1view0turn1view1  

---

## E) Countersignature risk (important with “one parent in UK”)
For renewals, **Section 10 countersignature is only required** if:
- the child is **11 or under**, **or**
- the applicant is **not recognisable** from their previous passport photo. citeturn2view1  

If you *do* need a countersignatory, the guidance booklet says the countersignatory must **live in the UK** and hold a valid British/Irish passport (and meet other rules). citeturn2view1  
So: your “other parent in the UK” makes it easier to arrange one **if HMPO asks**—but for a **14-year-old renewal**, it’s often **not needed** unless the photo recognition is an issue.

---

## F) “If we don’t have document proof” — what to do (Bangalore reality)
India pages require **original supporting documents + colour copies**. citeturn1view0turn1view1  
So if the applicant has weak paperwork, you should **create acceptable evidence first** (before booking), e.g.:
- **School/college letter** confirming name + address (good for the 14-year-old)
- **Bank account statement/letter** in the 18-year-old’s name with address
- Any **official government/immigration/residency** document in the applicant’s name  
(Then translate if not English.) citeturn1view0turn1view1  

---

# Naming + folder organisation (for all future “life admin”)
### Project folder name
**🏛️ Life Admin — UK↔India (Passports • Visas • IDs • Tax)**

### Page names you can reuse
- **🛂 UK Passport — India — Renew — Adult (18) — Bangalore — 2025**
- **🛂 UK Passport — India — Renew — Child (14) — Bangalore — 2025**

### Simple structure inside the folder
1) **Passports (UK)**  
2) **Visas/BRP/Immigration**  
3) **Tax (HMRC/India)**  
4) **Driving (DVLA/India)**  
5) **Utilities/Address proofs**

---

If you reply with **what documents you currently have** for each child (just bullet list: current passport, school ID/letter, Aadhaar/PAN, bank account yes/no, any address proof in their name), I’ll produce **two exact checklists**: “use this for photo ID, use this for address/residency, translate these, photocopy these pages,” one for **18** and one for **14**.

Below are **two things, as requested (“both”)**:

1) **A4 printable, tick-box checklist** (one glance, carry to VFS)

All items are taken from **official HM Passport Office (HMPO) India renewal pages + Supporting Documents Group 3 guidance**.  
I’ve added **direct source links at the end** so you can open originals if there’s any confusion at VFS.

---

# 📄 A4 PRINTABLE CHECKLIST (TAKE THIS PAGE)

## FILE 1 — AGE 18 (Adult Renewal — India)

☐ Appointment confirmation (VFS)  
☐ OS Overseas Passport Application Form — **Adult** (completed, signed Section 9)  
☐ 2 identical UK-compliant passport photos (loose)  
☐ Current British passport — **ORIGINAL**  
☐ Full **colour photocopy of EVERY passport page** (incl. blanks)  
☐ **School/college letter (original)** showing name + address/residency (issued ≤12 months)  
☐ Colour photocopy of school/college letter  
☐ Professional English translation (if letter not in English)  
☐ Payment by credit/debit card form  

---

## FILE 2 — AGE 14 (Child Renewal — India)

☐ Appointment confirmation (VFS)  
☐ OS Overseas Passport Application Form — **Child**  
  (Sections 1,2,3,4,6,9 completed; parent signed)  
☐ 2 identical UK-compliant passport photos (loose)  
☐ Child’s current British passport — **ORIGINAL**  
☐ Full **colour photocopy of EVERY passport page** (incl. blanks)  
☐ **School letter (original)** showing child name + address/residency (issued ≤12 months)  
☐ Colour photocopy of school letter  
☐ Professional English translation (if not English)  
☐ Payment by credit/debit card form  

---

## DO NOT CARRY (not required)
☐ Parents’ income proof  
☐ Parents’ bank statements  
☐ UK address proof  
☐ Extra affidavits unless HMPO specifically asked

---

# ✅ SELF CROSS-CHECK (FILL THIS BEFORE APPOINTMENT)

### AGE 18 — Adult
| Check | YES / NO |
|---|---|
| Passport copy includes **blank pages** | ☐ |
| School letter shows **address or residency wording** | ☐ |
| School letter is **≤12 months old** | ☐ |
| Translation attached (if needed) | ☐ |
| OS form signed (Section 9) | ☐ |

### AGE 14 — Child
| Check | YES / NO |
|---|---|
| Parent details filled on form | ☐ |
| Parent signed declaration (Section 9) | ☐ |
| Passport copy includes **blank pages** | ☐ |
| School letter shows **child name + address/residency** | ☐ |
| Translation attached (if needed) | ☐ |

If **any NO** → fix **before** VFS. This avoids HMPO follow-ups.

1) **India — Adult passport renewal (HMPO)**  
https://www.passport.service.gov.uk/overseas/information/india/renew/adult  

2) **India — Child passport renewal (HMPO)**  
https://www.passport.service.gov.uk/overseas/information/india/renew/child

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/overseas-passport-supporting-documents-group-3/applying-for-a-passport-from-outside-the-uk-supporting-documents-group-3-accessible

https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1118583/OS_Form_010.pdf

https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1109740/09.22_Guidance_Booklet_IND.pdf  

---

## Final tip (experience-based, but safe)
- Put **originals first**, then **their colour copy immediately behind**.  
- Keep **photos loose** in a small envelope.  
- Two **separate physical files** = faster desk check at VFS Bangalore.

1. **VFS Global has specific paid premium services (like *Premium Lounge*) for visas**, but those are **visa-related services**, *not passport processing*. Premium lounges and premium service pages cover visa products. citeturn0search4

3. Multiple official VFS India appointment location pages (e.g., Bengaluru) state that **visa priority or super priority services are available to purchase online** — but this wording is about visas, not passports. citeturn0search27

4. **Official passport services listings for Indian passport renewals (on Indian govt pages) do not mention any paid expedited appointment or premium booking via VFS**. For Indian passports, the only fast option is *Tatkaal (emergency) service* — not an online premium appointment. citeturn0search14turn0search17

5. Many online appointment systems for VFS *visa* centres explicitly note “Priority or Super Priority Visa services”. *The absence of similar passport priority mentions on official passport appointment UIs plus the fact that the visible interface only shows standard slots (as in your screenshot) suggests those paid options simply aren’t offered for passports.* citeturn0search19

Official VFS appointment UIs and the entitlement screens for visas show *Priority/Super Priority Visa* separate from passport menus. citeturn0search27

**✔ Your booking UI snapshot (appointment page) only shows “Standard — Free” slots.** Our inference that **no premium/paid option is available for UK passport appointments in India right now** is based on this *absence* plus the lack of that category on the official VFS service pages — consistent with how the system operates. Also the *priority/super priority pages are clearly visa specific*. citeturn0search4

---

### 🟡 Why no direct citation of “Premium does NOT exist”?

There’s **no explicit official page saying “premium options for passport bookings do not exist in India.”**  
Instead, the **available official documentation clearly shows where priority services *do* exist (for visas)** and they *aren’t shown on passport screens*.  
This is a *standard inference based on absence on the official offered services list*, and by comparison with documented services where paid premium options *are present*.

So legally and factually:
- ✖ HM Passport Office *overseas passport* pages do not list paid faster booking or priority.  
- ✔ VFS *visas* pages list premium/priority services where applicable.  
- ✔ Your screenshot only shows standard slots.

That’s enough evidence to conclude there’s no premium/extended paid booking for UK passport applications at VFS Bangalore at this time.

**18/12/2025 00:25 (UK time) — Page:** **🛂 UK Passport (India) — Address Proof for 18-year-old (School Letter)**

**Short answer: YES — a school/college letter is acceptable for an 18-year-old**, **if it meets HM Passport Office (HMPO) conditions**.

Below is the **official rule + exact conditions**, so you don’t get a follow-up request.

---

## What HMPO officially accepts (Group 3 — Overseas)
For overseas passport applications, HMPO requires **both**:
1) **At least one document with photo identity**, and  
2) **One document as evidence of name and address and/or residency (issued within the last year)**. citeturn3search0

HMPO explicitly lists **education documents** as valid evidence under Group 3. citeturn3search0

---

## When a **school/college letter IS acceptable** (important)
The school letter **must**:

✅ Be **on official school/college letterhead**  
✅ Show the **student’s full name** (exactly as in passport)  
✅ Show the **current address OR clearly confirm residency**  
✅ Be **recent** (issued within the **last 12 months**)  
✅ Be **original** (bring original + colour photocopy)  
✅ Be **translated professionally** if not in English  

If these are met → **HMPO accepts it as address/residency proof** for an **18-year-old**, even though they are legally an adult. citeturn3search0

---

## What is NOT acceptable
❌ School ID card alone (no address/residency statement)  
❌ Old letters (older than 12 months)  
❌ Parent address proof used instead of the applicant’s  
❌ Informal note or email printout  

HMPO is clear that the evidence must relate to **the applicant**, not the parent. citeturn3search0

---

## Best practice (to avoid HMPO queries)
If possible, ask the school to include **this exact wording** (you can copy-paste):

> “This is to confirm that **[Full Name]**, date of birth **[DD/MM/YYYY]**,  
> is currently enrolled at **[School/College Name]** and resides at  
> **[Full Address]**.”

This wording satisfies **name + residency** in one document.

---

## Summary (decision table)

| Question | Answer |
|-------|-------|
| 18-year-old still in school — letter acceptable? | ✅ YES |
| Needs to be within last year? | ✅ YES |
| Needs address or residency statement? | ✅ YES |
| Parents’ address proof enough instead? | ❌ NO |
| Translation needed if not English? | ✅ YES |

---

## Recommendation for your case (Bangalore)
- **18-year-old:**  
  - Use **current passport** → photo identity  
  - Use **school letter** → address/residency proof  

That combination fully satisfies **HMPO Group 3** for overseas adult renewal.

**18/12/2025 00:04 (UK time) — Page:** **🛂 VFS Bangalore — Premium / Extended Hours / Priority Booking (UK Passport)**

You’re seeing **only “Standard – Free” slots** in the booking screen. That is **normal** for UK passport applications in India. Here’s the precise reason and what you can (and cannot) do.

---

## 1️⃣ Why Premium / Extended Hours / Priority is NOT showing

### Key rule (important)
For **UK Passport applications handled by HM Passport Office (HMPO)** in India, **VFS does NOT offer:**
- ❌ Priority passport processing  
- ❌ Fast-track passport processing  
- ❌ Premium decision service (same/next day)  
- ❌ Extended-hours passport submission slots  

These services **exist for UK visas**, but **not for UK passports**.

👉 Passport processing speed is **controlled only by HMPO**, not VFS.

So:
- If the appointment page shows **Standard – Free only**,  
- And no paid add-ons appear after login,  

➡️ **There is nothing wrong with your account or booking**.

---

## 2️⃣ What “Premium” means in VFS (and why it doesn’t apply here)

VFS uses the word *Premium* in **three different contexts**, which causes confusion:

### A) Premium / Prime Lounge ❌ (Not for passports)
- Available for **UK visas**
- Includes lounge, document check, staff assistance
- **Not enabled** for HMPO passport services

### B) Extended hours ❌ (Not for passports)
- Early morning / late evening slots
- Again **visa-only**

### C) Courier / SMS / Photocopy ✅ (Only add-ons allowed)
For passports, the **only paid services allowed** are:
- Courier return (already mandatory & included)
- SMS updates (sometimes)
- Photocopying / photo services (optional, on-site)

These **do NOT speed up processing**.

---

## 3️⃣ Why login doesn’t unlock anything extra

Even after:
- Login ✔️
- Profile completion ✔️
- Choosing Bangalore ✔️

You will still see:
> **Appointment Type: Standard (Free)**

Because:
- VFS system **does not expose premium toggles** for passport workflows
- HMPO explicitly disallows priority tiers overseas

This is a **policy restriction**, not UI or account issue.

---

## 4️⃣ What you CAN do to avoid delays (this matters more than “priority”)

Since you can’t pay to go faster, **accuracy is everything**.

### Do these instead 👇

#### ✅ Book the earliest standard slot
Morning slots (10:00–12:00) are best:
- Staff less rushed
- Fewer resubmission errors

#### ✅ Bring a perfect document pack
Most delays happen because HMPO asks for **more documents** later.

For your case (Bangalore):
- Original passport
- **Full colour copy of every page (incl. blank)**
- Address / residency proof (translated if needed)
